_note: Figures follow the FSA's Safer Food, Better Business (SFBB) pack and the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013. Wales and Northern Ireland use the same chill and hot-holding limits. Scotland differs in places (for example reheating to 82 °C) and uses the CookSafe pack. Checklist wording is our plain-English version of the SFBB pages, not the FSA's own text.

fridge.label: Fridge
fridge.plain: Keep chilled food at 8 °C or below. That is the law in England. Aim for 5 °C or below.
fridge.targetText: Above the 5 °C target. Still legal, but turn the fridge down a little.
suggestions: Closed the door and checked the seal
Turned the thermostat down
Moved the food to another fridge
Checked again 30 minutes later
Threw away high-risk food that was above 8 °C for over 4 hours
Called an engineer
fridge._note: Chilled food may be above 8 °C once, for up to 4 hours (for example while serving or moving it). Over that, throw high-risk food away.

freezer.label: Freezer
freezer.plain: Keep frozen food at −18 °C or colder.
suggestions: Closed the lid or door properly
Moved the food to another freezer
Food still frozen hard, so kept it
Food had thawed: moved to the fridge and used within 24 hours
Threw the thawed food away
Called an engineer
freezer._note: −18 °C is the standard for frozen food storage and what most SFBB packs use. A short rise while defrosting or loading is normal; check again.

hot_hold.label: Hot holding
hot_hold.plain: Keep hot food at 63 °C or hotter. That is the law in England.
suggestions: Reheated the food until steaming hot (75 °C core)
Turned the unit up
Threw away food that was below 63 °C for over 2 hours
Moved the food to another unit
Called an engineer
hot_hold._note: Hot food may be below 63 °C once, for up to 2 hours. After that, reheat it once or throw it away.

probe.label: Cooking probe
probe.plain: Cook food until the centre reaches 75 °C. Probe the thickest part.
suggestions: Cooked it for longer and probed it again
Cut it into smaller pieces and cooked again
Checked the probe in iced and boiling water
Threw the food away
probe._note: SFBB uses 75 °C. Other safe time and temperature mixes: 70 °C for 2 minutes, 80 °C for 6 seconds. Some foods, such as rare beef, have their own safe method.

opening.title: Opening checks
opening.plain: Do these before you start work.

items.text: Fridges, chilled displays and freezers are working
Other equipment, such as the oven, is working
Staff are fit for work and in clean work clothes
Prep areas are clean and disinfected: worktops, boards, equipment
There is soap, paper towels and sanitiser
The probe thermometer works and is clean
No signs of pests

closing.title: Closing checks
closing.plain: Do these before you lock up.

items.text: Food past its use-by date is thrown away
Food is covered, labelled and put in the fridge or freezer
Dirty cloths are out for washing
Bins are emptied and have new bags
Prep areas are clean and disinfected
Floors are clean and clear
Fridges and freezers are working and at the right temperature

weekly.title: Weekly check
weekly.plain: Once a week, look back over the diary and the kitchen.

items.text: I read this week's diary. Problems are written down
The deep clean on the cleaning schedule is done
Stock is rotated: first in, first out
Fridge and freezer door seals are clean and not split
The probe thermometer is cleaned and its battery is OK

four_weekly.title: 4-weekly review
four_weekly.plain: Every 4 weeks, check your safe methods still match what you do.

items.text: Any serious or repeated problems are written down with what we did
New staff are trained in our safe methods
Any new suppliers are checked and listed
New dishes or methods have a safe method
New or changed equipment is noted
The cleaning schedule and products are up to date
Allergen information is up to date for every dish

pest.title: Pest check
pest.plain: Look for signs of mice, rats, insects and birds.

items.text: No droppings, gnaw marks or nests
No damaged packets or food spills in stores
No flies, cockroaches or other insects
No gaps around pipes, doors or windows
Fly screens and door strips are in place
Bins outside are closed and the area is clean

delivery.title: Delivery check
delivery.plain: Check every delivery before you put it away.

items.text: Packaging is clean and not damaged
Use-by and best before dates are OK
The van and driver looked clean
Food is labelled, including allergens
Chilled and frozen food was put away straight away

calibration.title: Probe check
calibration.plain: Test the probe in iced water and in boiling water.

items.text: Probe cleaned and disinfected before and after
Battery is OK

delivery.plain: Chilled food should arrive at 8 °C or below. Frozen food at −15 °C or colder.
suggestions: Rejected the delivery
Rejected the warm items only
Told the supplier
Probed again inside the pack
delivery._note: −15 °C on delivery is a common supplier tolerance (frozen food may warm a little in transit), not a legal limit. Check what your supplier agreed to.

calibration.plain: In iced water it should read −1 °C to 1 °C. In boiling water, 99 °C to 101 °C.
suggestions: Changed the battery and tested again
Stopped using this probe
Bought a new probe
Sent the probe back to the maker
calibration._note: SFBB suggests checking probes regularly; we remind every 4 weeks. Very high altitude lowers the boiling point slightly, which does not matter in the UK.

reminders.openBody: Take your fridge and freezer temperatures and tick the opening checks.
reminders.closeBody: Tick the closing checks before you lock up.
reminders.nagBody: Some temperatures or checks are not done yet. If you're closed today, say so in the app.

fhrs.plain: Inspectors give a score from 0 to 5. They look at three things. Your diary is the main proof for the third one.

elements.title: How food is handled
elements.detail: Is food prepared, cooked, cooled, reheated and stored safely?
tips: Probe cooked food and log it
Keep raw and ready-to-eat food apart

elements.title: Cleanliness and condition of the building
elements.detail: Are the kitchen, equipment and toilets clean and in good repair? Is there good light, air and hand washing?
tips: Tick the opening and closing checks
Fix broken seals and tiles quickly

elements.title: Managing food safety
elements.detail: Do you have a food safety system, such as SFBB, and do you keep records? Do staff know what to do?
tips: A corrective action for every bad reading

fhrs._note: This is the Food Hygiene Rating Scheme used in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scotland uses the Food Hygiene Information Scheme (Pass or Improvement Required).
